task_retrieval_key: An 80-year-old woman presented with difficulty in raising her right upper limb, progressive dyskinesia, and gait disorder. She had experienced neck pain for approximately 2 years and numbness in her extremities for about a year, both of which had worsened significantly before her visit. She could walk unassisted for less than 100 meters. Muscle weakness (manual muscle testing [MMT] score: 3) was observed in the entire right upper limb, while strength in the remaining limbs was normal. Hypesthesia was noted throughout the upper and lower limbs. Deep tendon reflexes were increased bilaterally in all limbs, with positive Hoffman’s and Wartenberg’s signs.

avoid: Do not treat an unsupported agent assertion as clinical evidence
recommended_check: Verify source binding before using the evidence for support or refute
